_comment: SYNTHETIC DOCUMENTATION FIXTURE. Companion to t905-2025-layout.json and
t905-2025-loci.json. Trench T905 and all 26 of these finds are invented.
None of it is archaeological evidence.
Twenty-six special finds, each with the locus, date, trench-book page,
coordinate and elevation a real one carries. FIVE of them are deliberately
inconsistent with the loci they are filed under -- two plot outside the
trench, two outside the sounding, two below the deepest surface their
locus ever reached. That is roughly the rate a season's findspots
actually misplace at, and it is the point of the fixture: a validator
that only ever sees clean input has never been shown to work.
Grid coordinates are signed: South and West negative. A trench book writes
'150.25E/24.75S'; that is (150.25, -24.75) here. Elevations are metres
above sea level on the corrected 25.23 mAE datum.
The recording method is the ordinary one: a plumb bob over the findspot, a
tape run at right angles to two baulk strings for the coordinates, and a
line level from the datum for the elevation.

finds.locus_source: Special Finds List only; the daily log entry omits the locus line

list.record: invented, in the form of a season Special Finds List
list.columns: SF#, Date, Pg#, Locus, Description, Cataloged?, Catalog #

coordinates.record: invented, in the form of a trench book's daily log entries
note: Every one of the 26 has a coordinate and an elevation. Only SF 1, 2
and 3 carry stated tolerances, because only those three came out of a
wheelbarrow rather than in situ: their coordinate is where the bucket
was filled, not where the object lay, and a record that does not say
so invites the number to be trusted as a findspot.

method.record: invented, in the form of a trench book's Methodology section
note: Plumb bob over the findspot, tape at right angles to two baulk
strings, line level from the datum. The Methodology quotes the datum

_known_problems: These are the deliberate defects. Each one is a mistake that a real
findspot record makes, placed here so the checks that catch them have
something to catch.
SF 8 AND SF 9 PLOT OUTSIDE THE TRENCH. T905 runs 150E to 155E. SF 8 is at
149.48E, 0.52 m west of the west baulk; SF 9 is at 149.18E, 0.82 m west of
it. Both are filed under Locus 2, which exists only inside the trench.
Their northings are in range and both were found in the northwest
quadrant, so the eastings are where the error is.
SF 16 PLOTS OUTSIDE THE SOUNDING AND BELOW IT. The Locus 6 sounding runs
153E-154E by 22S-24S and its floor at closing is 23.74-23.79 mAE. SF 16 is
recorded at 153.30E/21.21S -- 0.79 m north of the sounding -- and at 23.44
mAE, 0.30 m below the deepest point the sounding ever reached, and below
the surface of unexcavated Locus 8. The daily log places it in the
northern metre of the sounding, so the prose and both numbers disagree.
SF 17 PLOTS 0.45 m WEST OF THE SOUNDING, at 152.55E against a west edge of
153E, though its elevation of 23.76 mAE sits correctly within Locus 6. A
check on elevation alone would pass it.
SF 3'S ELEVATION IS 0.29 m BELOW ITS LOCUS. At 23.75 mAE it is below every
Locus 1 closing reading. It was recorded with SF 1 (24.56) and SF 2
(24.35) from the same wheelbarrow at the same nominal spot, on a day spent
lowering a spoil heap whose crest was at 24.70 mAE. Nothing on site was at
23.75 mAE that day. A check on plan position alone would pass it.
SF 20 AND SF 21 ARE MARKED 'Cataloged? No' AND GIVEN CATALOGUE NUMBERS
(CAT-0145, CAT-0146) in the same rows. The season conclusion refers to
both numbers as catalogued objects, so the flag is wrong, not the numbers.
SF 16 IS MARKED 'Cataloged? No' WITH NO NUMBER on the list, while the
Locus 6 form and description both give CAT-0126. The number is used here.
SF 20 AND SF 21 ARE 'frieze plaque fragments' on the list and in the daily
log, and 'sima cavetto fragments' in the season conclusion: two different
architectural terracotta types for the same two catalogue numbers.
SF 10 IS A 'Glass shard' on the list and in the daily log, and an obsidian
flake in the Lithics Summary -- where it is the trench's only lithic.
Obsidian is volcanic glass, so this is plausibly a re-identification
during study rather than a contradiction, but no record says so. If it is
glass, the season's lithic count is zero. Not every disagreement is an
error, and the record rarely distinguishes.
SF 11'S DATE DISAGREES BY ONE DAY between the list and the page of the
trench book it cites. The log date is used here.
SF 15'S STATED DEPTH DOES NOT REPRODUCE. The log says it lay ca. 13 cm
below the floor surface. Interpolating the Locus 6 opening surface at its
coordinates gives about 23.89 mAE, and the find is at 23.82, which is 7 cm.
The Locus 6 description likewise puts its Archaic material 15 to 20 cm
beneath the floor while grouping SF 15 with SF 20 and SF 21, which
recompute to about 24 cm. Depths quoted in prose and depths recomputed
from the recorded surfaces are not the same numbers, and the recomputed
ones are the ones with a provenance.
SF 22 HAS NO LOCUS IN THE DAILY LOG and one decimal place on its elevation
(23.6) where every other reading has two. The list assigns it Locus 7.
